key_insight: A symmetric semi-implicit projection scheme achieves second-order shallow-water time integration on the sphere while restricting stability by advection rather than fast waves.
engineering_relevance: The method supports larger time steps for spherical geophysical flow simulations, with advection subcycling requiring no additional implicit solves.
method: Use compatible finite elements to separate advection and wave dynamics.
Apply an explicit half-step, a DG-upwind SSPRK3 advection step, and an implicit half-step that projects velocity into H(div).
Solve the implicit wave system efficiently through hybridisation in Firedrake.
evidence_signal: Standard spherical shallow-water benchmarks show second-order convergence, stable results at Courant numbers up to 1 with two advection subcycles and second-order finite elements, and good parallel scaling.
watch_item: Reported stability is benchmark-specific; advection subcycling still must respect its CFL restriction and adds explicit computational work.
paper_title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
